source.snippet: Every product seems to go through constant UI churn that has no benefit to users other than changing around whitespace or refreshing the look. If you have a full time UX person they _must_ change the UI of your product otherwise there is no way to get promoted. That is just an unavoidable fact of incentive structures. As a company how can you avoid that issue? (4 points)

problem_statement: Companies with dedicated UX staff experience constant UI churn driven by promotion incentives rather than user need, wasting engineering resources and frustrating users with unnecessary changes.
target_segment: Engineering managers and CPOs at product companies with 10-200 employees who pay for dedicated UX headcount
notes: Pain is real and recurring in SaaS/product companies. Potential buyer: product ops tooling or design governance platforms. Weak direct willingness-to-pay signal in this item, but the problem maps to costly engineering rework — companies do pay for solutions that reduce wasted sprint cycles.
